title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240. Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/analysis issues are evident in the archived artifacts: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the execution artifacts. Interpreted conservatively, the results show that bounded GVR provides no additional verifier-detectable benefit when the generator+prompting combination already yields verifier-acceptable candidates on this synthetic workload; they do not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, or verifier. We document artifact-grounded reproducible next steps (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and extended verifier coverage) that follow directly from the archived preregistration and execution manifests.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate invariants (reachability, ACLs, workflow ordering). Prior literature therefore recommends verifier-interposed architectures and generate–verify–repair (GVR) loops to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to answer the research question: does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic-violation rates relative to a strong unconstrained baseline under a frozen experimental plan? Our contributions are (1) a fully archived preregistration (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) and deterministic execution on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks); (2) artifact-backed confirmatory statistics showing a null effect under the executed shared-generation semantics (n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0); (3) a concise statistical clarification about paired-test degeneracy when discordant counts are zero and how that interacts with the preregistered power argument; and (4) an explicit, artifact-grounded reconciliation documenting a preregistration–execution mismatch (shared_initial_candidate vs. power assumption of independent generation) and an unexecuted prespecified comparison (C vs B). We release the archived artifacts and describe reproducible next steps that can be executed using those artifacts.
sections.related_work: Three bodies of verified work motivate this study and frame interpretation. First, surveys and empirical studies document hallucination, fabrication, and incorrect structured outputs from LLMs across domains, motivating deterministic validators in operational pipelines (e.g., generate–verify literature and broad LLM surveys). Second, prior work on generate–verify–repair and constraint- or grammar-constrained decoding shows measurable improvements for mechanically checkable properties (compilation, syntax, test-passing) and suggests GVR as a practical mitigation in NetOps prototypes. Third, NetOps-specific efforts emphasize verifier-driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants) and human-in-the-loop governance for high-stakes changes. These prior findings justify evaluating whether an interposed verifier plus a bounded repair step reduces verifier-detected semantic violations. Unlike many prior systems reports or benchmarks that measure surface or syntactic correctness, our confirmatory design measured verifier-detectable semantic invariants in a preregistered paired framework. The authoritative bibliography and evidence map used to support these claims are archived with the execution artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The study preregistration (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) fixed the primary estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate). The confirmatory sample comprised N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). The preregistration specified two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B) with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025) and a paired McNemar two-sided exact test as the principal hypothesis test. Planned paired-bootstrap 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; these analysis parameters were archived and used by the registered analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1).
Execution contract and frozen parameters: Execution adhered to the archived adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested generator model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The deterministic validator used in scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial frozen semantics in the execution manifest record generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The preregistration artifact (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d) was archived prior to execution.
Design rationale and a preregistration–execution inconsistency: The preregistered power calculation and precision plan assumed independent per-condition generation (i.e., each arm would draw independent stochastic candidates), which creates within-pair discordance potential needed to detect paired differences. The archived execution instead used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across arms) to reduce model-call cost. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation file record this semantics; no amendment or recorded rationale changing the preregistration assumption appears in the archived artifacts. Because the change materially affects sensitivity and inference, we explicitly disclose it as an unresolved preregistration deviation supported by archived evidence (see Disclosure Statement). This reconciliation is reported here rather than deferred to provenance files so readers can evaluate the inferential consequence.
sections.results:
Accountanted execution (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate produced one generation per pair reused across arms); maximum_model_calls budget = 480 (execution_manifest). Representative per-task scoring artifacts and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ and show consistent validator outputs.
Primary confirmatory outcomes (registered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1): contingency counts: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded-only accepted), n01 = 0 (baseline-only accepted), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm the accounting and the reported numbers.
Repair diagnostics and usage: repair_applied = false for every episode; the bounded repair loop never triggered because the shared initial candidate satisfied the verifier predicates on every task. Representative scoring JSONs (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json) contain validator fields validation_before and validation_after with violation_count = 0 and validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The contamination_summary.csv and missingness_summary.csv report zero flags and zero failures.
Statistical clarification (degeneracy): The absence of discordant pairs (n10 = n01 = 0) makes the paired McNemar test degenerate: no within-pair disagreements exist to support a differential effect, hence the exact-test p = 1.00 and a collapsed bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0]. This degeneracy is deterministic given the archived contingency and arises irrespective of sample size; therefore the preregistered power calculation—premised on independent generation producing potential discordance—does not apply to the executed shared-generation design. The registered analysis executor and bootstrap parameters used in the archived run are recorded and reproduced exactly in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and artifact-grounded mechanisms. The null result observed (no discordance; identical acceptance in both arms) is artifact-supported and explained by two non-exclusive mechanisms evident in archived artifacts. First, task–verifier alignment: the synthetic task bank and verifier predicates created a distribution the generator+prompting combination could satisfy deterministically for the encoded invariants—hence no verifier-detectable defects existed for GVR to correct. Second, sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics: reusing a single generated candidate across arms removes stochastic per-arm variation and therefore the opportunity for GVR to demonstrate improvement; repairs are never invoked because both arms start from the same valid candidate.
Implications for evaluation design. If an evaluation aims to measure whether GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under realistic generator stochasticity, the evaluation must allow independent per-condition generation (restore discordance potential), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks designed to induce verifier failures, or test across multiple generator families and prompt variants. These artifact-grounded prescriptions follow directly from the preregistration and execution manifests: toggling independent_condition_generation to true and injecting the preregistered 10% golden tasks would implement the intended confirmatory design while preserving archived task manifests and RNG seeds.
Practical operational implications. Passing a deterministic verifier for a limited set of invariants does not imply operational safety beyond the verifier's coverage. Deployments that rely solely on a single verifier and bounded single-repair steps risk two failure modes: (i) oracle incompleteness (violations outside verifier scope) and (ii) overfitting repairs that satisfy the verifier but introduce undesirable operational side-effects. The artifacts document verifier scope (validation fields) and the limited repair budget; operational claims must be bounded accordingly.
Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison. The preregistration specified two primary comparisons (GVR vs unconstrained baseline and GVR vs schema-constrained baseline). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified C vs B comparison was not executed and no recorded rationale for its omission appears in the archived artifacts. We disclose this deviation explicitly and treat it as an unresolved procedural limitation that narrows the familywise inference.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-generation semantics, every initial candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n = 240 pairs), producing a null result (paired estimate = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.00; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Artifact-backed reconciliation shows that this null outcome is compatible with (a) a generator+prompting pairing that already satisfies the evaluated verifier predicates and (b) an executed shared-generation design that eliminates within-pair stochasticity. Because the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and because a prespecified comparison (C vs B) was not executed (no recorded rationale in artifacts), the null cannot be generalized beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, and shared-generation design. We release and document the authoritative archived artifacts so that reproductions can (i) switch to independent per-condition generation, (ii) inject adversarial/golden tasks, (iii) run multi-model comparisons, and (iv) expand verifier coverage—steps that are necessary to robustly evaluate GVR’s operational value beyond this narrow setting. All reported numbers and procedural statements in this paper are traceable to the archived execution and analysis artifacts cited below and summarized in the Disclosure Statement and analysis artifacts references.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
